items.title: Harold E. Peterson Interview, 1979-08-06
items.q: I know almost nothing about him. ... Oh man, I heard that band play.

ctx.x: Oh yes, oh, well played a little bit. I know almost nothing about him. Well, Harry Tarzan played, before I went out to the, uh, uh, the, uh, the, uh, the, uh, before I played before I had a band out at the, uh, Roadhouse out there, I heard him playing with a band and I think he was playing with- Jules Cherzaud was playing piano. I think Mary Brunesse was playing cornet in them days, Harry Tarzan clarinet. And I think it was George Treey on drums, played fine drums. one of my dad's students who played fine. He…
there and I read or heard somewhere that there was a fellow named Burt and he had the Five

Aces Down from Chicago. Do you know that? Oh man, I heard that band play. That's the band that I'm telling you about that when Boynie and I went over there they had some differences with the band. Yeah. Uh, Foxy Marriott, let's see if I can tell you the name of the piano player. Jesus, I believe, what was his name now? Gee whiz. Uh, Bob Sackerman played saxophone. Oh yeah, I met his niece. Well, Bob Sackerman played saxophone and I played with Bob later on when he came to New Orleans. He came to New Orleans to…
